proposals.title: Monorepo scaffold and build tooling
proposals.why_now: The repository contains no production code. Every subsequent proposal depends on a working TypeScript monorepo with the correct package topology (section 14.4), strict compiler settings, workspace tooling, and a CI pipeline skeleton. Nothing can be built or validated without this foundation.

acceptance_targets: docs/decisions/ADR-002-hash-function.md: specifies the hash function bit-by-bit (recommended: SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator), documents the rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) -> uint64 interface, and records the namespace isolation table

docs/decisions/ADR-004-rounding-enforcement.md: specifies how division without an explicit rounding mode becomes a compile-time or lint error, with the chosen enforcement mechanism (custom ESLint rule or branded type approach)

proposals.title: Write blocking ADRs for DEFINIR items required by FASE-1
proposals.why_now: ADR-002 marks the hash function as DEFINIR and requires it be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before implementation. ADR-009 requires its own ADR before CanonicalEncoder is written. ADR-004 marks technical enforcement of rounding modes as DEFINIR. All three unblock core package implementation and are prerequisites for FASE-1 acceptance. Writing them now costs little and unblocks the most work.

acceptance_targets: Branded types Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick are nominal (not assignable to each other or to raw number/bigint) and have validating constructors that reject non-integers and out-of-range values
rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) is a pure function, has no mutable state, and matches the algorithm specified in ADR-002 bit-for-bit

CanonicalEncoder serializes any valid domain value to bytes deterministically: same logical value produces same bytes, different logical value produces different bytes; rejects undefined, NaN, Infinity, -0 with errors not silent coercion
Division helpers require an explicit rounding mode argument at call site; calling without a mode fails at the type level or lint level per ADR-004

Unit tests cover: branded type rejection of wrong types, rand determinism across namespaces, canonical encoding of bigint vs safe integer, encoding of ordered vs unordered collections, and rejection of all forbidden values
All of core is pure: no imports from domain, world, application, narrative, or any impure module

proposals.title: Implement packages/core — branded types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, division helpers
proposals.why_now: Every other package depends on core. The branded numeric types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick) enforce ADR-003 at the type level. The positional RNG enforces ADR-002. The CanonicalEncoder is required by ADR-009 before any StateHash can be produced. Division helpers enforce ADR-004. Until core exists, world and domain cannot be built, and no invariant test can run.

proposals.title: Lint infrastructure — determinism and dependency boundary rules, CI-blocking
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires lint of determinism by default negation and lint of dependency boundaries to be active and blocking in CI before the phase is accepted. The earlier these rules are enforced, the fewer violations accumulate. Introducing them late means retrofitting every already-written module. The negation-default scope (all packages under packages/ are pure unless explicitly listed in lint.impure-packages) must be established before new packages are created.

proposals.title: Implement packages/world — price generator with two assets and two noise layers
proposals.why_now: The price generator is the load-bearing structure of the entire simulation. INV-02 (direct price query equals tick-by-tick advance) is the most important test in the project per the specification. The generator must be correct before the tick loop, the ledger, or the replay tool can be meaningfully validated. Implementing it with two assets and two noise layers (as scoped in FASE-1) produces the first falsifiable determinism test and establishes the fixed-point arithmetic patterns all subsequent world computation inherits.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository is empty of production code. Only benchmark infrastructure files (.gitkeep, README, spec copy) exist. No packages, no tooling, no CI, no ADRs, no application code.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The monorepo itself does not exist. There is no TypeScript project, no package structure, no build tooling, and no CI pipeline. Every FASE-1 deliverable is blocked on the foundational scaffold.

warnings: Three DEFINIR items in the spec must be resolved by ADR before their corresponding implementation can begin: (1) the hash function for rand() in ADR-002, (2) the CanonicalEncoder spec in ADR-009, and (3) the technical enforcement mechanism for rounding modes in ADR-004. Implementing core before these ADRs are written violates spec section 19 and produces implementation choices that may need to be reversed.

FASE-1 acceptance requires INV-29 (Electron contextIsolation, nodeIntegration: false, sandbox: true in all modes including development). The Electron application shell must be created with these settings active from its first commit. Retrofitting security settings after the fact is high-risk and has caused INV-29 regressions in comparable projects.

The octave count, block periods, and amplitude parameters for the price generator are marked DEFINIR (section 5.1). These parameters must be recorded in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before implementation. Choosing values ad hoc without recording them makes the price generator unreproducible across environments and violates the baseline freeze required by FASE-1 acceptance.
